title: Trade agreement
description: One source file per legal instrument under data/trade_agreements/<ID>.yaml. Records agreements, parties, status, dates and catalogue identifiers only: no trade values, tariff lines, depth scores or rankings. A record either lists its parties or links to the intblock that holds them (intblock); a linked record takes its name and Wikidata id from that intblock, its links from that intblock followed by its own, and its dates too unless it sets signed, in_force or ended itself (an organization's founded date is not always the signature of its trade agreement).

id.description: Stable identifier, uppercase for new records. Shares one namespace with intblock ids; equal to an intblock id (which may be mixed case, such as AfCFTA) only when intblock names that id.

name.description: English name of the agreement, as used by the parties or the depositary. Omitted on a record linked to an intblock.

agreement_type.description: fta: free trade agreement (goods, often with services). customs_union: common external tariff. pta: reciprocal partial-scope or preferential agreement. preference_scheme: non-reciprocal preferences granted to beneficiary countries (GSP, AGOA). services: services only. investment: standalone treaty whose main object is the promotion, protection or facilitation of investment (bilateral investment treaty, FIPA, investment protection agreement, plurilateral investment treaty); an agreement with an investment chapter keeps its FTA, PTA or services type. trade_relations: most-favoured-nation or normal trade relations treatment without preferential tariff commitments (trade relations agreements, bilateral trade agreements, treaties of commerce). digital: digital trade or digital economy agreement. framework: framework or trade and investment framework agreement without tariff commitments. other: an instrument a catalogue lists that is none of these (compact of free association, strategic partnership).

status.description: proposed: under study. negotiating: negotiations launched. suspended: negotiations launched and then suspended, paused or put on hold, not formally ended; not for agreements in force. signed: signed, not in force. in_force: in force, or applied provisionally, for at least two parties. terminated: was in force and ended. abandoned: negotiated or signed, never in force, no longer pursued. superseded: replaced by another agreement (superseded_by).

in_force.description: Date of definitive entry into force for at least two parties. Left out while the agreement is only applied provisionally (provisional_application). Catalogue records taken from WTO RTA-IS or ADB ARIC may hold a provisional date here, because those catalogues do not tell the two apart.

provisional_application.description: Date from which at least two parties applied the agreement provisionally, before or without its entry into force.

parties.description: Parties to the agreement. A bloc that signs as one party (the EU) is one intblock party. For catalogue-level records a bloc may stand for its member states.

role.description: Set only on a preference_scheme record, where every party needs it. grantor: gives the preferences. beneficiary: receives them. Reciprocal agreements have no role, because each of their parties both grants and receives.

provisional_application.description: Date from which the agreement applied provisionally between this party and the others, when it differs from the record or the record has none.

intblock.description: The intblock that holds the roster of an agreement with three or more parties. Parties, name and Wikidata id are read from it, and its links come before the record's own; dates too, unless the record sets them.

parent.description: Set only on a preference_scheme record: the id of the preference scheme this record belongs to. That is a framework (GSP), or the national scheme of the same grantor (EU-GSP is the parent of GSP+ and Everything but Arms).

unctad_iia_id.description: UNCTAD Investment Policy Hub IIA Navigator treaty identifier (international-investment-agreements/treaties/<type>/N/...).

unts_registration.description: United Nations Treaty Series registration number (I-NNNNN for registered treaties, II-NNN for filed and recorded ones), from the UN Treaty Collection.

wto_pta_ids.description: PTA ids of the rows in the WTO Preferential Trade Arrangements Database that describe this legal instrument. It is a list because several members can notify one instrument: Armenia, Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic and Russia each notify the EAEU tariff preferences.

gptad_id.description: World Bank Global Preferential Trade Agreements Database (GPTAD) agreement id (dispIDS in the GPTAD search).

dta_id.description: World Bank Deep Trade Agreements (DTA) database agreement id (WB ID, the WBID column of the DTA content files).

type.description: treaty_text: the full text of the agreement (depositary, party government or a catalogue copy such as a GPTAD PDF); the registry stores the URL, not the text.

notes.description: Legal facts: accessions, suspensions, supersession, conflicts between sources. Not trade volumes.

instruments.description: Instruments that amend or add to the agreement among its parties: upgrade and amending protocols, supplements, supplementary agreements, early harvest arrangements, joint committee decisions. They do not change the agreement's own status or dates. An agreement that replaces this one, an agreement concluded under an umbrella treaty with its own parties, and an accession are not instruments. See openspec/changes/add-trade-agreement-instruments.

verification.description: official: parties and dates checked against the treaty text, a depositary or a party government. catalogue: taken from WTO RTA-IS, the WTO Preferential Trade Arrangements Database, ADB ARIC, GPTAD, the UNCTAD IIA Navigator or the UN Treaty Series only (a GPTAD record cites another source for its status).

id.description: Unique within the record and never changed once published, such as upgrade-2018 or supplement-10.

kind.description: amending_protocol: amends the agreement (upgrade, optimization, enhancement, second phase, supplement). supplementary_agreement: a further agreement under it covering a new area. early_harvest: an early harvest arrangement. joint_committee_decision: a decision of the agreement's joint body amending it or its annexes. exchange_of_letters: letters that launch or settle part of the agreement. other: any other change a source lists.

name.description: English name as used by the source.

status.description: negotiating: negotiations launched. signed: signed, not in force. in_force: in force for at least two parties; its in_force date is the date it applied to all parties, or the first date when the source gives only that, and staggered dates go in notes. terminated: was in force and ended, or was replaced by a later instrument. abandoned: never in force, no longer pursued.

notes.description: Legal facts, such as staggered entry into force or conflicting dates between sources.
